paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Jehoshaphat had troops in every fortified city, and that's fine, a king should guard his kingdom. But the line that carries the whole passage is this one: "the LORD was with Jehoshaphat because he walked in the earlier ways of his father David." (2 Chronicles 17:3) The strength that mattered most wasn't the soldiers. It was who was standing beside him.

Now look at what a king who seeks God does with his power. He "sought the God of his father and walked by His commandments," and his "heart took delight in the ways of the LORD." (2 Chronicles 17:4, 6) Then he sent a team out to teach the people, carrying the Book of the Law of the LORD. (2 Chronicles 17:7, 9) A man whose heart delights in God wants everybody else to know the Word too, and that's the same reason I'm happy to see you in my bakery.

So here's what it means for you, baker. Get ready by getting into the Word, one passage at a time, and let your heart enjoy it instead of treating it like a chore. Strong ovens, full cookie boxes and a good plan are all nice, but they're no substitute for walking with the LORD. And Jehoshaphat's story isn't over, so keep your apron on.
